Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the inherited rollout evidence, and both relevant skill instructions. I’ll then make one policy candidate, document its evidence trail, update the reusable control lesson, and run the prescribed contract checks.

The workspace confirms a single editable policy file and forbids local CFD. I’m now applying the fish-control bookshelf protocol and the visual-first protocol before forming the architecture hypothesis; the latter requires inspecting both wake views, not just metrics.

All four sampled rollouts are the same deterministic capture (three identical policies plus one acceleration clamp that never activates), and their keyframe sheets are byte-identical. There is therefore no sampled visual failure to compare; I’ll use the captured sheet as the finite reference and the inherited, quantified near-miss/guard regressions as the failure comparison, and I’ll state that evidence limitation explicitly in the notes.

The visual evidence shows self-propulsion from quiescent water: an initially compact wake becomes a long, coherent alternating sheet, stays attached through the broad turn, and bends with the final approach. The controller is already successful, so the useful opening is route efficiency—reducing unnecessary late curvature without disturbing the posterior-lag carrier—not more thrust. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a mechanism-level way to express that in existing normalized body-frame feedback.

I’m recording the pre-edit diagnosis and hypothesis now, as required by the visual-first skill. The chosen shelf transfer is a closed-loop “speed recovery” modulation: briefly raise cadence only when measured forward speed is low and the target is nearly aligned in the body frame, then remove it as speed builds or a redirect begins. This preserves the proven curvature and posterior-lag mechanisms while testing a distinct feedback capability.

The candidate loads successfully and produces finite commands on a representative aligned-start state. I’m now revising the durable lesson: the sampled acceleration projection changes only issued commands at the same downstream clamp and leaves every applied state/flow trajectory value unchanged, so it is a validated interface equivalence—not a performance improvement—and repeated copies should trigger a new bounded feedback test.

The policy, provenance notes, and durable guidance are all updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s prescribed check-runner now; it will run only the guidance, policy-contract, schema, and boundary checks—no CFD.

The dedicated check-runner could not start because its fixed `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable for this account. I’m preserving the required validation by running the exact three commands from its configuration myself, separately and without CFD.

All three prescribed checks pass: durable-guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/finite action, and editable-file boundary. I’m doing one final read-only check of the new gate’s off-regions and the final file set; no CFD will be run.

Implemented exactly one candidate: an alignment-gated, low-speed cadence recovery that preserves the proven completion-gated redirect and posterior-lag carrier.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

All prescribed checks passed: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/schema, and workspace boundary. Additional gate tests confirmed it activates during aligned low-speed motion and disables at cruise speed or during redirects. No CFD was run.
